# A ball times a limb, two-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_scale_2_full_entry` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, that contains $x a$ for every $x \in X$, with $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$. A ball may also be the whole line or the empty set.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, x a : x \in X \,\}.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c_x = c_{x0} + c_{x1}$, $c_w = c_{w0} + c_{w1}$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X * a` | `Ball<T, 2>`, `T` | `Ball<T, 2>` |  |
| `a * X` | `T`, `Ball<T, 2>` | `Ball<T, 2>` |  |
| `X *= a` | `Ball<T, 2>`, `T` | `Ball<T, 2>` |  |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- $a$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- **B1.** The result $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball, the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- **B2.** $Z$ is empty exactly when $X$ is empty.
- **B3.** If $Z$ is a finite ball, then $X$ is a finite ball and $a$ is finite, and $\lvert (x a) - c_w\rvert \le r_w$ for all real $x$ with $\lvert x - c_x\rvert \le r_x$.
- **B4.** If $X$ is a finite ball and $a$ is finite and $\lvert (\lvert c_x\rvert + r_x) a\rvert \le 2^{e_{\max} - 2}$, then $Z$ is a finite ball. The conditions are on the exact values of the operands, and $2^{e_{\max}}$ is the overflow threshold of `T`, just above its largest finite number: $2^{e_{\max} - 2}$ is $2^{1022}$ for `double`, $2^{126}$ for `float`.
- It follows that in every case $Z$ contains $x a$ for every $x \in X$: the whole line contains every real number, and an empty operand has no points.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_scale_2_full_entry_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallFinite.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallFinite.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_scale_2_full_entry_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_scale_2_full_entry_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** ball_scale_2 on its guarded scalar, then the fix-up of ball_scale_2_full (rule R3, the factors of a fused operation). **License:** core: as ball_scale_2; fix-up: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_scale_2_full_entry.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_scale_2_full_entry.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`ball_scale_2`](ball_scale_2.md).

```
# Ball<T, 2> * T, T * Ball<T, 2> and *= (rule R3, the factors of a fused operation:
# architecture.md): a passes through guard, then ball_scale_2_full. ball_scale_2_full only multiplies
# a (in the core's mul_2_1 and in the product of the radius), which R3 alone does not guard; but a
# compiler that sees the leading limb of the center to be 1 fuses a product a = y z of the program
# into the fms of the core's two_prod, as it does in mul_2_1 (Apple clang 21 under
# -ffp-contract=fast, measured there). The guard is placed here, not in ball_scale_2: the core is
# reached only through ball_scale_2_full, so one guard either way, and the listings of both, with
# their theorems of Milestone 1, are kept. rx is the radius of a ball of the library. The fix-up of
# ball_scale_2_full is written out here, not called, so that the printer puts it behind a branch as
# for every full Ball kernel (cpp.branch takes a kernel's own selects): called, it was computed on
# every product, 2.6 times the time of a dependent chain with Apple clang (measured). Its claims are
# those of ball_scale_2_full: they say of a only whether it is finite and its value, which the
# guard keeps.

ga             = guard(a)
(cz0, cz1, rz) = ball_scale_2(cx0, cx1, rx, ga)
e              = eq(rx, rx)
az             = abs(cz0)
f1             = lt(az, const inf)
f2             = lt(rz, const inf)
f              = and(f1, f2)
c0             = select(f, cz0, 0)
c1             = select(f, cz1, 0)
r              = select(f, rz, const inf)
cw0            = select(e, c0, rx)
cw1            = select(e, c1, rx)
rw             = select(e, r, rx)
```

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
